quotes.text: Prompts are not user input. They're runtime policy. They shape behavior. They constrain scope, and they change faster than change management can track.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes prompts as runtime logic that needs the same discipline as configuration.

quotes.text: Mean time to explain. Is the time it takes your best people to answer a single, humiliating question? Why did the system do that?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines the episode's central metric in one memorable sentence.

quotes.text: Agent First Architecture is not a new diagram style. It's a discipline for keeping probabilistic reasoning from infecting deterministic execution.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core design principle for building agents that stay controllable.

quotes.text: In architectural terms, MCP is not an integration convenience. It is a tool distribution system and every distribution system becomes an entropy accelerator unless you force contracts around what gets distributed
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balanced take on MCP that names both its value and its governance risk.

quotes.text: If the organization can't cleanly kill an agent, it can't claim it controls agents. It just accumulates them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sharp test for whether an organization really controls its agent estate.

chapters.title: AI as an operating model, not a feature
Scenarios: Copilot, Power Platform and Azure
Agent-first architecture and the control plane

takeaways: Rolling out Copilot and agents is an operating model shift from deterministic SaaS to probabilistic orchestration, not a feature deployment.
Mean time to explain — how fast you can reconstruct why an agent did something — is the risk metric that decides whether agents can scale.
Agent-first architecture keeps reasoning probabilistic but forces execution through deterministic, owned boundaries: agent identity, tool contracts, telemetry, lifecycle and kill switches.
hook: Your Copilot rollout looks like progress, yet your architecture feels less stable every quarter. This episode is for Microsoft 365, Power Platform and Azure leaders who are scaling agents and want to understand why behavior drifts even when nothing was changed. You learn the mean-time-to-explain metric, three real-world entropy scenarios and an agent-first design that keeps execution legible and owned.
